39:47.ar: وَلَوۡ أَنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ مَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَمِيعࣰ ا وَمِثۡلَهُۥ مَعَهُۥ لَٱفۡتَدَوۡاْ بِهِۦ مِن سُوٓءِ ٱلۡعَذَابِ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۚ وَبَدَا لَهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَمۡ يَكُونُواْ يَحۡتَسِبُونَ
39:47.en: And though those who do wrong possess all that is in the earth, and therewith as much again, they verily will seek to ransom themselves therewith on the Day of Resurrection from the awful doom; and there will appear unto them, from their Lord, that wherewith they never reckoned

39:48.ar: وَبَدَا لَهُمۡ سَيِّـَٔاتُ مَا كَسَبُواْ وَحَاقَ بِهِم مَّا كَانُواْ بِهِۦ يَسۡتَهۡزِءُونَ
39:48.en: And the evils that they earned will appear unto them, and that whereat they used to scoff will surround them

39:49.ar: فَإِذَا مَسَّ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ ضُرࣱّ دَعَانَا ثُمَّ إِذَا خَوَّلۡنَٰهُ نِعۡمَةࣰ مِّنَّا قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أُوتِيتُهُۥ عَلَىٰ عِلۡمِۭۚ بَلۡ هِيَ فِتۡنَةࣱ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَهُمۡ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
39:49.en: Now when hurt toucheth a man he crieth unto Us, and afterward when We have granted him a boon from Us, he saith: Only by force of knowledge I obtained it. Nay, but it is a test. But most of them know not

39:50.ar: قَدۡ قَالَهَا ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ فَمَآ أَغۡنَىٰ عَنۡهُم مَّا كَانُواْ يَكۡسِبُونَ
39:50.en: Those before them said it, yet (all) that they had earned availed them not

39:51.ar: فَأَصَابَهُمۡ سَيِّـَٔاتُ مَا كَسَبُواْۚ وَٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ مِنۡ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ سَيُصِيبُهُمۡ سَيِّـَٔاتُ مَا كَسَبُواْ وَمَا هُم بِمُعۡجِزِينَ
39:51.en: But the evils that they earned smote them; and such of these as do wrong, the evils that they earn will smite them; they cannot escape

39:52.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَبۡسُطُ ٱلرِّزۡقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيَقۡدِرُۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يُؤۡمِنُونَ
39:52.en: Know they not that Allah enlargeth providence for whom He will, and straiteneth it (for whom He will). Lo! herein verily are portents for people who believe

70:11.ar: يُبَصَّرُونَهُمۡۚ يَوَدُّ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُ لَوۡ يَفۡتَدِي مِنۡ عَذَابِ يَوۡمِئِذِۭ بِبَنِيهِ
70:11.en: Though they will be given sight of them. The guilty man will long to be able to ransom himself from the punishment of that day at the price of his children

70:12.en: And his spouse and his brother

70:13.en: And his kin that harboured him

70:14.ar: وَمَن فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَمِيعࣰ ا ثُمَّ يُنجِيهِ
70:14.en: And all that are in the earth, if then it might deliver him

39:16.ar: لَهُم مِّن فَوۡقِهِمۡ ظُلَلࣱ مِّنَ ٱلنَّارِ وَمِن تَحۡتِهِمۡ ظُلَلࣱۚ ذَٰلِكَ يُخَوِّفُ ٱللَّهُ بِهِۦ عِبَادَهُۥۚ يَٰعِبَادِ فَٱتَّقُونِ
39:16.en: They have an awning of fire above them and beneath them a dais (of fire). With this doth Allah appal His bondmen. O My bondmen, therefor fear Me

18:103.en: Say: Shall We inform you who will be the greatest losers by their works

18:104.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ ضَلَّ سَعۡيُهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَهُمۡ يَحۡسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمۡ يُحۡسِنُونَ صُنۡعًا
18:104.en: Those whose effort goeth astray in the life of the world, and yet they reckon that they do good work

39:8.ar: ۞وَإِذَا مَسَّ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ ضُرࣱّ دَعَا رَبَّهُۥ مُنِيبًا إِلَيۡهِ ثُمَّ إِذَا خَوَّلَهُۥ نِعۡمَةࣰ مِّنۡهُ نَسِيَ مَا كَانَ يَدۡعُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهِ مِن قَبۡلُ وَجَعَلَ لِلَّهِ أَندَادࣰ ا لِّيُضِلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦۚ قُلۡ تَمَتَّعۡ بِكُفۡرِكَ قَلِيلًا إِنَّكَ مِنۡ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلنَّارِ
39:8.en: And when some hurt toucheth man, he crieth unto his Lord, turning unto Him (repentant). Then, when He granteth him a boon from Him he forgetteth that for which he cried unto Him before, and setteth up rivals to Allah that he may beguile (men) from his way. Say (O Muhammad, unto such an one): Take pleasure in thy disbelief a while. Lo! thou art of the owners of the Fire

28:76.ar: ۞إِنَّ قَٰرُونَ كَانَ مِن قَوۡمِ مُوسَىٰ فَبَغَىٰ عَلَيۡهِمۡۖ وَءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلۡكُنُوزِ مَآ إِنَّ مَفَاتِحَهُۥ لَتَنُوٓأُ بِٱلۡعُصۡبَةِ أُوْلِي ٱلۡقُوَّةِ إِذۡ قَالَ لَهُۥ قَوۡمُهُۥ لَا تَفۡرَحۡۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡفَرِحِينَ
28:76.en: Now Korah was of Moses' folk, but he oppressed them; and We gave him so much treasure that the stores thereof would verily have been a burden for a troop of mighty men. When his own folk said unto him: Exult not; lo! Allah loveth not the exultant

28:77.ar: وَٱبۡتَغِ فِيمَآ ءَاتَىٰكَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلدَّارَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۖ وَلَا تَنسَ نَصِيبَكَ مِنَ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ وَأَحۡسِن كَمَآ أَحۡسَنَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيۡكَۖ وَلَا تَبۡغِ ٱلۡفَسَادَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُفۡسِدِينَ
28:77.en: But seek the abode of the Hereafter in that which Allah hath given thee and neglect not thy portion of the world, and be thou kind even as Allah hath been kind to thee, and seek not corruption in the earth; lo! Allah loveth not corrupters

28:78.ar: قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أُوتِيتُهُۥ عَلَىٰ عِلۡمٍ عِندِيٓۚ أَوَلَمۡ يَعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَدۡ أَهۡلَكَ مِن قَبۡلِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلۡقُرُونِ مَنۡ هُوَ أَشَدُّ مِنۡهُ قُوَّةࣰ وَأَكۡثَرُ جَمۡعࣰ اۚ وَلَا يُسۡـَٔلُ عَن ذُنُوبِهِمُ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُونَ
28:78.en: He said: I have been given it only on account of knowledge I possess. Knew he not that Allah had destroyed already of the generations before him men who were mightier than him in strength and greater in respect of following? The guilty are not questioned of their sins

89:15.ar: فَأَمَّا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ إِذَا مَا ٱبۡتَلَىٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ فَأَكۡرَمَهُۥ وَنَعَّمَهُۥ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّيٓ أَكۡرَمَنِ
89:15.en: As for man, whenever his Lord trieth him by honouring him, and is gracious unto him, he saith: My Lord honoureth me

89:16.ar: وَأَمَّآ إِذَا مَا ٱبۡتَلَىٰهُ فَقَدَرَ عَلَيۡهِ رِزۡقَهُۥ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّيٓ أَهَٰنَنِ
89:16.en: But whenever He trieth him by straitening his means of life, he saith: My Lord despiseth me

kfmD85Aupmw.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat Az-Zumar (39:47-52)
kfmD85Aupmw.one_line: Ransoming oneself with the whole earth, and 'I was given it only because of my knowledge': vanity, blessings as trials, and sincerity in what comes to you.
kfmD85Aupmw.summary: Before reaching the closing verses he loves most, he takes up overlooked ones. Everyone is a slave to something, and you are as strong as what you serve; the sincere hold the world in their hands, not their hearts, and stay content in illness, like Imran ibn Husayn bedridden for thirty years and Ahmed Deedat paralysed for sixteen, though such sincerity is Allah's gift. Verses 47-48 bring warning after much encouragement: the wrongdoer would hand over the earth twice over without bargaining, because what he never reckoned appears: the evil of his earnings, including what he mocked by his deeds. Verse 49 shows vanity: rescued from harm and later blessed, a person says 'I was given it only because of my knowledge', like Qarun, who did work hard. Blessings come through doors Allah opens, often years after a prayer, and each is a trial, not proof of love. The same deed, such as building masjids, can be billions of good deeds or bad ones depending on whether credit goes to Allah. Claiming the credit is hidden shirk, associating yourself with Him. Sincerity covers both what you give and how you see what comes to you; praise others' efforts but attribute your own to Allah.

outline.heading: Opening
Verses people overlook
outline.gist: The surah's closing verses are among the Quran's most beautiful, so the ones before them are neglected despite their importance.

outline.heading: Master yourself first
outline.gist: Az-Zumar is about obedience of the heart; as al-Junayd said, whoever masters himself is better able to master anything else.

outline.heading: Everyone is a slave; choose to whom
outline.gist: We are created as servants; even a ruler adored by others is a slave of power, money or comfort.

outline.heading: As strong as what you worship
outline.gist: You fear losing whatever you serve; the servant of Allah fears only losing his bond with Him.

outline.heading: The world in your hand, not your heart
outline.gist: Enjoy what comes and give it to Allah and family; if it goes you do not grieve, and everything is subjected to you, not you to it.

outline.heading: The happiness of a heart filled with Allah
outline.gist: Kings and pleasure-seekers cannot know this joy; living hostage to fortune is a life not worth living.

outline.heading: Imran ibn Husayn: thirty years bedridden
outline.gist: Unable to rise, he kept teaching and said: something Allah chose for me, shall I not accept it for myself?

outline.heading: Deedat and a teacher who kept teaching
outline.gist: Deedat debated from a hospital bed for sixteen years by eye and finger; one of his teachers was carried from lesson to lesson.

outline.heading: Sincerity is a gift, not an attainment
outline.gist: You walk the path, but a heart filled only with Allah is something He grants.

outline.heading: Verses 47-48 recited
outline.gist: The wrongdoers would ransom themselves with all the earth and as much again.

outline.heading: The more you own, the harder to give it up
outline.gist: Someone with only a phone gives it easily to escape punishment; someone owning a city starts to bargain.

outline.heading: On that Day he gives it all at once
outline.gist: Without bargaining he hands over two earths, and would offer his children, wife and clan.

outline.heading: What they never reckoned
outline.gist: Ihtisab is calculation, like the Ottoman tax assessor; they thought their small wrongs were nothing, and every calculation changes.

outline.heading: A 'law' only Allah can say
outline.gist: Humans say 'if I had' in ignorance; Allah knows exactly what would happen.

outline.heading: Sincerity through warning
outline.gist: Most of the surah encouraged; this passage warns that you cannot imagine what awaits the insincere.

outline.heading: Mocking by deeds
outline.gist: Haqa means surrounding then descending; one may never mock the Fire in words yet mock it by repeating what Allah threatened.

outline.heading: Those who think they do well
outline.gist: Some arrive on the Day pleased with themselves and find their deeds wrong; others know exactly where they are going.

outline.heading: Verse 49 recited
outline.gist: When harm touches him he calls on Us; when We grant him a blessing he says it was by his knowledge.

outline.heading: Personal, not forgetful
outline.gist: Verse 8 described forgetting and taking rivals; here 'Us' makes it personal, and khawwala means permission to use a blessing for a time.

outline.heading: Vanity versus arrogance: Qarun
outline.gist: Kibr compares you with others, 'ujb with yourself; Qarun answered his people with these very words.

outline.heading: Blessings come through doors He opens
outline.gist: Qarun truly worked hard, but nothing falls on anyone's head; Allah inspires the work, connects you with people and opens the opportunity.

outline.heading: 'Then': answered years later
outline.gist: Wealth ten years on may be the answer to a prayer made in hardship; 'innama' restricts, as in 'deeds are only by intentions'.

outline.heading: No, it is a trial
outline.gist: 'Innama' denies Allah's share; the blessing was only a test of what you would do with it.

outline.heading: Without sincerity, vanity moves in
outline.gist: People put 'this is from my Lord's favour' on a sign but, when asked, credit themselves.

outline.heading: Those before them said it too
outline.gist: Some who said it seemed to prosper until death; the verse points back to the Day when their earnings become evil.

outline.heading: Building masjids for nothing
outline.gist: The same deed can raise you in Paradise or sink you; masjids built with 'I achieved it' bring the builder nothing though people benefit.

outline.heading: Effort is real; the question is how you see it
outline.gist: Study, business and relationships require effort; others should credit your effort while you credit Allah.

outline.heading: We have it backwards
outline.gist: We call others' success luck and our own skill; the Prophet honoured people's achievements while the achiever credits Allah sincerely.

outline.heading: Giving is not love, withholding not hatred
outline.gist: Blessing and deprivation are both trials of whether you will be grateful or arrogant, patient or bitter.

outline.heading: Verses 51-52 recited
outline.gist: The evils of their earnings struck them, and Allah extends and restricts provision; the wording links back to the opening scene.

outline.heading: One deed, opposite outcomes
outline.gist: Billions of good deeds or bad ones differ only by intention at the start and crediting Allah throughout.

outline.heading: He could have stopped you at any moment
outline.gist: He protected you along the way with intelligence, life and land He gave; provision is extended and restricted as a trial.

outline.heading: Hidden shirk: associating yourself with Allah
outline.gist: Allah says He granted it; saying 'I was given it' contradicts Him, a lie to people, to yourself and to your Lord.

outline.heading: A word that would pollute the sea
outline.gist: When Aisha remarked on Safiyyah's height, the Prophet said that word mixed into the sea would pollute it.

outline.heading: Sincerity in what comes to you
outline.gist: Be sincere in what you give and in seeing that what comes to you is from Allah; thank the giver while knowing the gift is His.

outline.heading: Outro

4:105.ar: إِنَّآ أَنزَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ لِتَحۡكُمَ بَيۡنَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِمَآ أَرَىٰكَ ٱللَّهُۚ وَلَا تَكُن لِّلۡخَآئِنِينَ خَصِيمࣰ ا
4:105.en: Lo! We reveal unto thee the Scripture with the truth, that thou mayst judge between mankind by that which Allah showeth thee. And be not thou a pleader for the treacherous

4:106.ar: وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرِ ٱللَّهَۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ غَفُورࣰ ا رَّحِيمࣰ ا
4:106.en: And seek forgiveness of Allah. Lo! Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful

4:107.ar: وَلَا تُجَٰدِلۡ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخۡتَانُونَ أَنفُسَهُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ مَن كَانَ خَوَّانًا أَثِيمࣰ ا
4:107.en: And plead not on behalf of (people) who deceive themselves. Lo! Allah loveth not one who is treacherous and sinful

4:108.ar: يَسۡتَخۡفُونَ مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَا يَسۡتَخۡفُونَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ وَهُوَ مَعَهُمۡ إِذۡ يُبَيِّتُونَ مَا لَا يَرۡضَىٰ مِنَ ٱلۡقَوۡلِۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ بِمَا يَعۡمَلُونَ مُحِيطًا
4:108.en: They seek to hide from men and seek not to hide from Allah. He is with them when by night they hold discourse displeasing unto Him. Allah ever surroundeth what they do

4:109.ar: هَٰٓأَنتُمۡ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ جَٰدَلۡتُمۡ عَنۡهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا فَمَن يُجَٰدِلُ ٱللَّهَ عَنۡهُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ أَم مَّن يَكُونُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَكِيلࣰ ا
4:109.en: Ho! ye are they who pleaded for them in the life of the world. But who will plead with Allah for them on the Day of Resurrection, or who will then be their defender

4:110.ar: وَمَن يَعۡمَلۡ سُوٓءًا أَوۡ يَظۡلِمۡ نَفۡسَهُۥ ثُمَّ يَسۡتَغۡفِرِ ٱللَّهَ يَجِدِ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣰ ا رَّحِيمࣰ ا
4:110.en: Yet whoso doeth evil or wrongeth his own soul, then seeketh pardon of Allah, will find Allah Forgiving, Merciful

4:111.ar: وَمَن يَكۡسِبۡ إِثۡمࣰ ا فَإِنَّمَا يَكۡسِبُهُۥ عَلَىٰ نَفۡسِهِۦۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمࣰ ا
4:111.en: Whoso committeth sin committeth it only against himself. Allah is ever Knower, Wise

4:112.ar: وَمَن يَكۡسِبۡ خَطِيٓـَٔةً أَوۡ إِثۡمࣰ ا ثُمَّ يَرۡمِ بِهِۦ بَرِيٓـࣰٔ ا فَقَدِ ٱحۡتَمَلَ بُهۡتَٰنࣰ ا وَإِثۡمࣰ ا مُّبِينࣰ ا
4:112.en: And whoso committeth a delinquency or crime, then throweth (the blame) thereof upon the innocent, hath burdened himself with falsehood and a flagrant crime

4:113.ar: وَلَوۡلَا فَضۡلُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡكَ وَرَحۡمَتُهُۥ لَهَمَّت طَّآئِفَةࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡ أَن يُضِلُّوكَ وَمَا يُضِلُّونَ إِلَّآ أَنفُسَهُمۡۖ وَمَا يَضُرُّونَكَ مِن شَيۡءࣲۚ وَأَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَعَلَّمَكَ مَا لَمۡ تَكُن تَعۡلَمُۚ وَكَانَ فَضۡلُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡكَ عَظِيمࣰ ا
4:113.en: But for the grace of Allah upon thee (Muhammad), and His mercy, a party of them had resolved to mislead thee, but they will mislead only themselves and they will hurt thee not at all. Allah revealeth unto thee the Scripture and wisdom, and teacheth thee that which thou knewest not. The grace of Allah toward thee hath been infinite

4:114.ar: ۞لَّا خَيۡرَ فِي كَثِيرࣲ مِّن نَّجۡوَىٰهُمۡ إِلَّا مَنۡ أَمَرَ بِصَدَقَةٍ أَوۡ مَعۡرُوفٍ أَوۡ إِصۡلَٰحِۭ بَيۡنَ ٱلنَّاسِۚ وَمَن يَفۡعَلۡ ذَٰلِكَ ٱبۡتِغَآءَ مَرۡضَاتِ ٱللَّهِ فَسَوۡفَ نُؤۡتِيهِ أَجۡرًا عَظِيمࣰ ا
4:114.en: There is no good in much of their secret conferences save (in) him who enjoineth almsgiving and kindness and peace-making among the people. Whoso doeth that, seeking the good pleasure of Allah, We shall bestow on him a vast reward

4:115.ar: وَمَن يُشَاقِقِ ٱلرَّسُولَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ ٱلۡهُدَىٰ وَيَتَّبِعۡ غَيۡرَ سَبِيلِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ نُوَلِّهِۦ مَا تَوَلَّىٰ وَنُصۡلِهِۦ جَهَنَّمَۖ وَسَآءَتۡ مَصِيرًا
4:115.en: And whoso opposeth the messenger after the guidance (of Allah) hath been manifested unto him, and followeth other than the believer's way, We appoint for him that unto which he himself hath turned, and expose him unto hell - a hapless journey's end

4:135.ar: ۞يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُونُواْ قَوَّٰمِينَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ شُهَدَآءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡ أَوِ ٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ وَٱلۡأَقۡرَبِينَۚ إِن يَكُنۡ غَنِيًّا أَوۡ فَقِيرࣰ ا فَٱللَّهُ أَوۡلَىٰ بِهِمَاۖ فَلَا تَتَّبِعُواْ ٱلۡهَوَىٰٓ أَن تَعۡدِلُواْۚ وَإِن تَلۡوُۥٓاْ أَوۡ تُعۡرِضُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣰ ا
4:135.en: O ye who believe! Be ye staunch in justice, witnesses for Allah, even though it be against yourselves or (your) parents or (your) kindred, whether (the case be of) a rich man or a poor man, for Allah is nearer unto both (them ye are). So follow not passion lest ye lapse (from truth) and if ye lapse or fall away, then lo! Allah is ever Informed of what ye do

RJjHSlUWO_g.title: The Story of the Stolen Shield
RJjHSlUWO_g.one_line: The theft of Rifa'ah's shield and the framing of a Jewish man, and how An-Nisa 105-115 put justice above tribe and faith.
RJjHSlUWO_g.summary: He sets the passage in An-Nisa (4:105-115) in the sixth year after the Hijrah, a year of social crises that he argues weighed on the Prophet more than battles. He then tells the story narrated by Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man: Qatadah's elderly uncle Rifa'ah, newly Muslim, has food and a valuable shield stolen from his shed. Qatadah traces it to the Banu Ubayriq brothers, one of them a known hypocrite, and the case threatens to reopen the old Aws-Khazraj feud. The brothers bury the shield in the yard of a Jewish man, Zayd ibn al-Samin, and come to the Prophet indignant. The evidence points to Zayd, and the Prophet rebukes Qatadah, until revelation comes in the night telling him not to plead for the traitors. He walks through the verses: people hide from people but not from Allah, the door of forgiveness, the gravity of pinning one's own sin on an innocent, and the only kinds of secret counsel that hold good. The lesson is that the Quran exonerated a non-Muslim and exposed a Muslim even at the cost of tribal peace, because justice is what matters. Linking this to 4:135, he asks the audience whether they could testify against a parent or themselves, contrasting this with the Western right not to incriminate oneself.

outline.heading: Context: the socially difficult sixth year
outline.gist: The verses came in the sixth year, a year of social crises such as the slander incident and the marriage to Zaynab, which he argues were harder on the Prophet than battle.

outline.heading: Qatadah and his uncle Rifa'ah
outline.gist: Introduces the narrator Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man and his elderly, nearly blind uncle Rifa'ah, who accepted Islam late after long encouragement, and notes that not everyone in Madinah was Muslim.

outline.heading: The theft of the food and the shield
outline.gist: Rifa'ah stores grain and a costly shield in his shed; it is broken into overnight, and the loss of the shield upsets him most.

outline.heading: Qatadah investigates
outline.gist: Fearing for his uncle's new faith, Qatadah follows a trail of spilled wheat to a neighbourhood where a poor family had cooked food that night.

outline.heading: The Banu Ubayriq and the hypocrite Bashir
outline.gist: The suspects are three brothers, one a known hypocrite who wrote paid poetry against the companions, yet hypocrites were never named and were treated as Muslims.

outline.heading: The Aws-Khazraj feud
outline.gist: Qatadah reports to the Prophet; he explains the decades of raids between the two tribes that the Prophet worked to end and that this case could reignite.

outline.heading: The feud flares at the minbar
outline.gist: When the Prophet asked from the minbar who would defend him against a man harming his family, men of the two tribes nearly came to blows.

outline.heading: The brothers plot a cover-up
outline.gist: Seeing Qatadah asking questions, Bashir asks his brothers to bear false witness; a cousin refuses to lie to the Prophet but agrees to stay silent.

outline.heading: Framing Zayd ibn al-Samin
outline.gist: They first try to blame a fierce Muslim, Labid, who threatens them, then bury the shield in the yard of a quiet Jewish man and accuse him before the Prophet.

outline.heading: The evidence and the Prophet's rebuke of Qatadah
outline.gist: An inquiry finds the shield in Zayd's yard; the Prophet rebukes Qatadah for accusing a Muslim household without proof and intends to clear the brothers publicly.

outline.heading: Night revelation: do not plead for the traitors
outline.gist: Jibril comes at night: the Book was sent to judge justly, the Prophet must not defend those who betray themselves and should seek forgiveness, having only followed the evidence.

outline.heading: Hiding from people but not from Allah
outline.gist: They conceal their night plotting from people while Allah is with them; those who argue for them now cannot argue for them on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: Repentance, and the sin of blaming an innocent
outline.gist: Whoever wrongs himself and seeks forgiveness finds Allah forgiving, but one who commits a wrong and pins it on an innocent carries a baseless slander and clear sin.

outline.heading: Allah's favour protecting the Prophet from being misled
outline.gist: A group tried to mislead the Prophet but could only harm themselves; Allah gave him the Book, wisdom and knowledge he did not have.

outline.heading: The only good in secret counsel
outline.gist: Most private conspiring holds no good except quietly arranging charity, a kindness, or reconciliation between people long at odds.

outline.heading: Bashir's apostasy and following other than the believers' way
outline.gist: Bashir left for Makkah and died fighting with Quraysh; the verse warns that one who opposes the Prophet after guidance is left to his chosen path.

outline.heading: Justice above tribe and faith
outline.gist: The Quran would not let a night pass with an innocent non-Muslim accused, even if it exposed a Muslim and inflamed the tribal feud, because justice is what matters in Islam.

outline.heading: Stand firm for justice even against yourselves
outline.gist: He links the story to the command a few verses later to testify for Allah even against oneself, parents and relatives, rich or poor.

outline.heading: Could you testify against someone you love?
outline.gist: Hypothetical cases, such as a hated neighbour robbed by your brother or your mother in a collision, test whether we would hesitate to tell the truth.

outline.heading: Contrast with the right not to self-incriminate
outline.gist: Western legal ethics allow a person not to incriminate himself, while the Quran obliges testimony even against oneself; he asks whether Muslims actually live this.

outline.heading: Rifa'ah gives the shield away
outline.gist: Once the shield was returned Rifa'ah gave it in charity, showing his faith had not been shaken by being wronged by Muslims, unlike people who leave the deen over a stolen pair of shoes.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Justice and refusing oppression
themes.note: Justice is the overriding value: the Quran cleared a Jewish man and exposed a Muslim, and believers must testify even against themselves and family.

themes.label: Quranic stories and their lessons
themes.note: Narrates the background story of the stolen shield in detail before reading the verses against it.

themes.label: Truthfulness and honesty
themes.note: Committing a wrong and pinning it on an innocent is a baseless slander and a clear sin.

themes.label: Hypocrisy (nifaq)
themes.note: Known hypocrites were never named or treated differently in Madinah; Bashir's later apostasy revealed him.

themes.label: Unity of the ummah
themes.note: The Prophet worked to end the Aws-Khazraj feud, which old loyalties kept threatening to reignite.

themes.label: Muslim identity and life in the West / Canada
themes.note: Islamic ethics of testimony go further than the Canadian and American norm against self-incrimination.

themes.label: Eman: faith, certainty, doubt
themes.note: A believer's faith should not hinge on being wronged by other Muslims.

quran.point: Be upholders of justice and witnesses for Allah even against yourselves, parents and relatives.

hadith.gist: Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man's account of his uncle's stolen shield, the Banu Ubayriq, and the revelation of the An-Nisa verses
The Prophet asked from the minbar who would defend him against a man harming his family, and men of Aws and Khazraj nearly fought

maxims: All that matters in Islam is that justice is served
If you hesitate even a second, you have not understood the deen

stories.who: Rifa'ah, Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man and the Banu Ubayriq
stories.point: A theft by Muslims was covered up by framing an innocent outsider; revelation refused to let it stand.

stories.who: Zayd ibn al-Samin, the Jewish man framed for the theft
stories.point: The Quran exonerated a non-Muslim from a hostile community over a Muslim, because truth outranks group loyalty.

stories.who: The Prophet judging by the evidence
stories.point: A human judge can only follow the evidence; he is told to seek forgiveness for nearly defending the guilty.

stories.who: Bashir of the Banu Ubayriq
stories.point: Opposing the Prophet after the truth was clear led him to apostasy and a bad end.

stories.who: Rifa'ah giving the shield in charity
stories.point: His faith stayed firm despite being wronged by fellow Muslims.

contemporary: The Canadian and American criminal justice systems and the right not to incriminate oneself
takeaways: Speak the truth and stand for justice even when it harms you or your family
Never let tribal, ethnic or religious loyalty decide who you believe is guilty
Do not accuse anyone without evidence, and never shift your own wrong onto an innocent
Use private gatherings only for charity, kindness and reconciling people
Do not let being wronged by Muslims shake your faith

2:152.ar: فَٱذۡكُرُونِيٓ أَذۡكُرۡكُمۡ وَٱشۡكُرُواْ لِي وَلَا تَكۡفُرُونِ
2:152.en: Therefore remember Me, I will remember you. Give thanks to Me, and reject not Me

31:12.ar: وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَا لُقۡمَٰنَ ٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ أَنِ ٱشۡكُرۡ لِلَّهِۚ وَمَن يَشۡكُرۡ فَإِنَّمَا يَشۡكُرُ لِنَفۡسِهِۦۖ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ حَمِيدࣱ‏
31:12.en: And verily We gave Luqman wisdom, saying: Give thanks unto Allah; and whosoever giveth thanks, he giveth thanks for (the good of) his soul. And whosoever refuseth - Lo! Allah is Absolute, Owner of Praise

76:1.ar: هَلۡ أَتَىٰ عَلَى ٱلۡإِنسَٰنِ حِينࣱ مِّنَ ٱلدَّهۡرِ لَمۡ يَكُن شَيۡـࣰٔ ا مَّذۡكُورًا
76:1.en: Hath there come upon man (ever) any period of time in which he was a thing unremembered

76:2.ar: إِنَّا خَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ مِن نُّطۡفَةٍ أَمۡشَاجࣲ نَّبۡتَلِيهِ فَجَعَلۡنَٰهُ سَمِيعَۢا بَصِيرًا
76:2.en: Lo! We create man from a drop of thickened fluid to test him; so We make him hearing, knowing

76:3.ar: إِنَّا هَدَيۡنَٰهُ ٱلسَّبِيلَ إِمَّا شَاكِرࣰ ا وَإِمَّا كَفُورًا
76:3.en: Lo! We have shown him the way, whether he be grateful or disbelieving

14:7.ar: وَإِذۡ تَأَذَّنَ رَبُّكُمۡ لَئِن شَكَرۡتُمۡ لَأَزِيدَنَّكُمۡۖ وَلَئِن كَفَرۡتُمۡ إِنَّ عَذَابِي لَشَدِيدࣱ‏
14:7.en: And when your Lord proclaimed: If ye give thanks, I will give you more; but if ye are thankless, lo! My punishment is dire

31:31.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱلۡفُلۡكَ تَجۡرِي فِي ٱلۡبَحۡرِ بِنِعۡمَتِ ٱللَّهِ لِيُرِيَكُم مِّنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّكُلِّ صَبَّارࣲ شَكُورࣲ‏
31:31.en: Hast thou not seen how the ships glide on the sea by Allah's grace, that He may show you of His wonders? Lo! therein indeed are portents for every steadfast, grateful (heart)

34:13.ar: يَعۡمَلُونَ لَهُۥ مَا يَشَآءُ مِن مَّحَٰرِيبَ وَتَمَٰثِيلَ وَجِفَانࣲ كَٱلۡجَوَابِ وَقُدُورࣲ رَّاسِيَٰتٍۚ ٱعۡمَلُوٓاْ ءَالَ دَاوُۥدَ شُكۡرࣰ اۚ وَقَلِيلࣱ مِّنۡ عِبَادِيَ ٱلشَّكُورُ
34:13.en: They made for him what he willed: synagogues and statues, basins like wells and boilers built into the ground. Give thanks, O House of David! Few of My bondmen are thankful

4:147.ar: مَّا يَفۡعَلُ ٱللَّهُ بِعَذَابِكُمۡ إِن شَكَرۡتُمۡ وَءَامَنتُمۡۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ شَاكِرًا عَلِيمࣰ ا
4:147.en: What concern hath Allah for your punishment if ye are thankful (for His mercies) and believe (in Him)? Allah was ever Responsive, Aware

6:53.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ فَتَنَّا بَعۡضَهُم بِبَعۡضࣲ لِّيَقُولُوٓاْ أَهَٰٓؤُلَآءِ مَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِم مِّنۢ بَيۡنِنَآۗ أَلَيۡسَ ٱللَّهُ بِأَعۡلَمَ بِٱلشَّٰكِرِينَ
6:53.en: And even so do We try some of them by others, that they say: Are these they whom Allah favoureth among us? Is not Allah best Aware of the thanksgivers

jJ8F9hDsYS0.speaker_note: Inferred, not certain: no name given, but the delivery is unlike the sheikh's (full English khutbat al-hajah, measured formal register, 'attitude of gratitude', no London or community references, no personal anecdotes or rants)
jJ8F9hDsYS0.title: Gratitude as a Way of Life
jJ8F9hDsYS0.one_line: Gratitude is the opposite of kufr and half of faith, shown on the tongue, in the heart and through the limbs. Adopt it as a way of life.
jJ8F9hDsYS0.summary: The khatib opens by saying hardship affects our physical, mental and spiritual wellbeing, and that shifting perspective changes how we experience it. He grounds gratitude in the Quran: Allah pairs shukr with kufr as opposites, so at its root disbelief is ingratitude toward the One who gave everything. Luqman was given wisdom to be grateful, humans were created from nothing and shown the two paths of gratitude and ingratitude, and gratitude brings certain and continuing increase. Drawing on Ibn al-Qayyim, he describes gratitude at three levels: praise on the tongue, witnessing and love in the heart, and obedience with the limbs. He adds Ibn al-Qayyim's five foundations, including humility, love and not using blessings in what Allah dislikes. Umar wept on hearing a man ask to be among the grateful few. The khatib recommends the Prophet's morning and evening dua acknowledging that every blessing is from Allah alone. In religion, look to those above you; in worldly matters, look to those below you. Patience and gratitude are the two halves of faith. Allah has no reason to punish those who are grateful and believe. He closes with narrations on thanking people who do you good and speaking of Allah's blessings.

outline.heading: Opening
Hardship and a shift in perspective
outline.gist: Trials and catastrophes affect us physically, mentally and spiritually, but shifting our perspective and attitude makes all the difference to how we experience them.

outline.heading: Remember Me and be grateful: shukr against kufr
outline.gist: Al-Baqarah 2:152 commands remembrance and gratitude and forbids ingratitude, placing shukr and kufr as opposites.

outline.heading: At its root, kufr is ingratitude
outline.gist: We usually set kufr against iman, but its essence is ingratitude: turning one's back on the One who gave everything, from health to sustenance. The response is an attitude of gratitude.

outline.heading: Luqman's wisdom: gratitude benefits the grateful
outline.gist: Luqman 31:12: Allah gave Luqman wisdom to be grateful; whoever gives thanks benefits himself, and whoever is ungrateful, Allah is free of need and praiseworthy.

outline.heading: Two paths: grateful or ungrateful
outline.gist: Al-Insan 76:1-3: man was nothing, then created from a mixed drop, given hearing and sight, and shown the way, grateful or ungrateful. Gratitude must be chosen as a way of life, seeing the blessings that always outnumber the hardships.

outline.heading: If you are grateful, I will increase you
outline.gist: Ibrahim 14:7: the emphatic form makes the increase certain and continuous. The severe punishment for ingratitude is stated as a warning, not as a direct condition, and Allah remains merciful and forgiving.

outline.heading: The ships at sea: signs for the patient and grateful
outline.gist: Using our faculties to know and obey Allah is how we draw near. Luqman 31:31: the ships sailing by Allah's blessing are signs for every sabbar and shakur, both emphatic forms, linking patience and gratitude.

outline.heading: Level one: gratitude on the tongue
outline.gist: Ibn al-Qayyim defines gratitude on three levels; the first is acknowledging and praising Allah's blessings with the tongue, which alone is not enough.

outline.heading: Level two: witnessing and love in the heart
outline.gist: The heart bears witness to the blessings and then loves the One who gave them, as a sound heart loves whoever does it good, and no one does more good than Allah.

outline.heading: Level three: obedience with the limbs
outline.gist: Hands, eyes, ears and tongue are a trust; gratitude of the limbs is using them in obedience, in ways that draw you near to Allah.

outline.heading: The five foundations of gratitude
outline.gist: Ibn al-Qayyim builds gratitude on humility before the One thanked, love for Him, acknowledging His blessings, praising Him for them, and not using them in what He dislikes.

outline.heading: Umar and the grateful few
outline.gist: Umar heard a man pray to be among the few; learning it came from Saba 34:13, few of My servants are truly grateful, he wept. Strive to be shakur, constantly grateful, not merely shakir.

outline.heading: The morning and evening dua of gratitude
outline.gist: Whoever says in the morning, 'O Allah, whatever blessing has come to me is from You alone, without partner; Yours is the praise and thanks,' has given the day's thanks, and likewise at night: a mercy, since we cannot count the blessings.

outline.heading: Look up in religion, down in worldly matters
outline.gist: A hadith he flags as weak but whose meaning scholars accept: whoever looks in religion to those better and strives to match them, and in worldly matters to those with less and thanks Allah, is recorded as patient and grateful.

outline.heading: The reverse: complacent in religion, regretful in the world
outline.gist: Looking down in religion breeds self-satisfaction, as with someone who prays five times and compares himself with one who does not; looking up in worldly matters breeds regret, and such a person is not recorded among the patient and grateful.

outline.heading: Faith is half patience, half gratitude
outline.gist: Patience holds you back from tempting disobedience; gratitude keeps you doing acts of obedience, thankful for being guided to them. The two together make up faith.

outline.heading: Interlude
Why would Allah punish the grateful believer?
outline.gist: The Quran brings gratitude and faith together: An-Nisa 4:147 asks why Allah would punish you if you are grateful and believe, since you are fulfilling your purpose.

outline.heading: Does Allah not know best the grateful?
outline.gist: Al-An'am 6:53: when disbelievers ask why Allah favoured poor believers, the answer is that He knows best who is grateful; the grateful are chosen for His favour.

outline.heading: Repay a favour, or praise the giver
outline.gist: Narrated by al-Bukhari: whoever receives a favour should repay it, or at least praise the giver, which is thanks; staying silent is ingratitude.

outline.heading: Whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah
outline.gist: In a narration he flags as weak but sound in meaning: whoever does not thank for little will not thank for much, because gratitude is a way of being; and whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah.

outline.heading: Speaking of Allah's blessings is gratitude
outline.gist: Speaking of Allah's blessings is gratitude and leaving it is ingratitude; the congregation is a mercy and division a punishment. He closes asking to be among the grateful and patient.

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation
themes.note: Shukr is the opposite of kufr, a chosen way of life, practised by tongue, heart and limbs, and rewarded with increase.

themes.label: Patience (sabr) and perseverance
themes.note: Patience and gratitude are paired: look up in religion and down in worldly matters. Faith is half of each.

themes.label: Eman: faith, certainty, doubt
themes.note: The Quran pairs gratitude with faith; Allah has no reason to punish those who hold both, and He knows best who is grateful.

themes.label: Mental health, anxiety and emotional wellbeing
themes.note: Shifting perspective toward blessings eases the mental and spiritual toll of hardship.

themes.label: Character and manners (akhlaq)
themes.note: Whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah. Repay a favour, or at least praise the person.

quran.point: Remember Me and I will remember you, be grateful and do not be ungrateful: shukr and kufr as opposites.
Luqman was given wisdom to be grateful. Gratitude benefits the grateful, and Allah is free of need.
Man was nothing, then created and given hearing and sight, and shown the way, grateful or ungrateful.
If you are grateful I will surely increase you. The emphatic form signals certain, continuing increase.
The ships sailing by Allah's blessing, that He may show you His signs, are signs for every patient, grateful person.
Few of My servants are truly grateful, the verse behind the man's dua that made Umar weep.
Why would Allah punish you if you are grateful and believe?
Is Allah not most aware of the grateful? The grateful are the ones chosen for His favour.

hadith.gist: Whoever says in the morning, 'O Allah, whatever blessing has come to me is from You alone, without partner; Yours is the praise and thanks,' has fulfilled the day's gratitude, and likewise at night.
Two traits get a person recorded as patient and grateful: in religion, looking to those above and striving to match them; in worldly matters, looking to those below and thanking Allah.
hadith.source: Tirmidhi (chain noted as weak by the khatib)

hadith.gist: Faith is two halves: half patience and half gratitude.
Whoever receives a favour should repay it, or at least praise the giver. Staying silent is ingratitude.

Whoever does not thank for little will not thank for much. Whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah. Speaking of Allah's blessings is gratitude, and unity is mercy while division is punishment.
hadith.source: Ahmad and others (weakness noted by the khatib)

maxims: An attitude of gratitude
At its essence, kufr is ingratitude
Gratitude is a way of life
Blessings always outnumber the hardships

stories.who: Umar in the marketplace
stories.point: A man asked Allah to make him among the few. Learning it meant the few who are grateful, Umar wept at his own shortfall: strive to be among the constantly grateful.

takeaways: Say the morning and evening dua acknowledging that every blessing is from Allah alone
Show gratitude on the tongue, in the heart and by using your limbs in obedience
In religion look to those above you, and in worldly matters to those below you
Thank and praise the people who do you good
Reframe hardships by looking for the blessings that always outnumber them

68:17.ar: إِنَّا بَلَوۡنَٰهُمۡ كَمَا بَلَوۡنَآ أَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ إِذۡ أَقۡسَمُواْ لَيَصۡرِمُنَّهَا مُصۡبِحِينَ
68:17.en: Lo! We have tried them as We tried the owners of the garden when they vowed that they would pluck its fruit next morning

68:18.en: And made no exception (for the Will of Allah)

68:19.ar: فَطَافَ عَلَيۡهَا طَآئِفࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكَ وَهُمۡ نَآئِمُونَ
68:19.en: Then a visitation from thy Lord came upon it while they slept

68:20.en: And in the morning it was as if plucked

68:21.en: And they cried out one unto another in the morning

68:22.ar: أَنِ ٱغۡدُواْ عَلَىٰ حَرۡثِكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰرِمِينَ
68:22.en: Saying: Run unto your field if ye would pluck (the fruit)

68:23.en: So they went off, saying one unto another in low tones

68:24.ar: أَن لَّا يَدۡخُلَنَّهَا ٱلۡيَوۡمَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّسۡكِينࣱ‏
68:24.en: No needy man shall enter it to-day against you

68:25.en: They went betimes, strong in (this) purpose

68:26.en: But when they saw it, they said: Lo! we are in error

68:28.ar: قَالَ أَوۡسَطُهُمۡ أَلَمۡ أَقُل لَّكُمۡ لَوۡلَا تُسَبِّحُونَ
68:28.en: The best among them said: Said I not unto you: Why glorify ye not (Allah)

68:29.ar: قَالُواْ سُبۡحَٰنَ رَبِّنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَٰلِمِينَ
68:29.en: They said: Glorified be our Lord! Lo! we have been wrong-doers

68:30.en: Then some of them drew near unto others, self-reproaching

68:31.en: They said: Alas for us! In truth we were outrageous

68:32.ar: عَسَىٰ رَبُّنَآ أَن يُبۡدِلَنَا خَيۡرࣰ ا مِّنۡهَآ إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا رَٰغِبُونَ
68:32.en: It may be that our Lord will give us better than this in place thereof. Lo! we beseech our Lord

68:33.ar: كَذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡعَذَابُۖ وَلَعَذَابُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ أَكۡبَرُۚ لَوۡ كَانُواْ يَعۡلَمُونَ
68:33.en: Such was the punishment. And verily the punishment of the Hereafter is greater if they did but know

68:10.en: Neither obey thou each feeble oath-monger

68:12.en: Hinderer of the good, transgressor, malefactor

5:116.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ يَٰعِيسَى ٱبۡنَ مَرۡيَمَ ءَأَنتَ قُلۡتَ لِلنَّاسِ ٱتَّخِذُونِي وَأُمِّيَ إِلَٰهَيۡنِ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِۖ قَالَ سُبۡحَٰنَكَ مَا يَكُونُ لِيٓ أَنۡ أَقُولَ مَا لَيۡسَ لِي بِحَقٍّۚ إِن كُنتُ قُلۡتُهُۥ فَقَدۡ عَلِمۡتَهُۥۚ تَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي نَفۡسِي وَلَآ أَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي نَفۡسِكَۚ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ عَلَّٰمُ ٱلۡغُيُوبِ
5:116.en: And when Allah saith: O Jesus, son of Mary! Didst thou say unto mankind: Take me and my mother for two gods beside Allah? he saith: Be glorified! It was not mine to utter that to which I had no right. If I used to say it, then Thou knewest it. Thou knowest what is in my mind, and I know not what is in Thy Mind. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Knower of Things Hidden

m-c-Ru4YFBI.title: Quranic Stories: The People of the Orchard
m-c-Ru4YFBI.one_line: Three sons who planned to withhold their generous father's harvest from the poor lose their orchard, a merciful lesson that they inherited a value, not land.
m-c-Ru4YFBI.summary: The sheikh tells the story of the owners of the orchard in Surat al-Qalam, likely the first Quranic story the Companions heard. A generous farmer in Yemen opened his orchard to the poor every harvest before picking it. His three sons, wanting the wealth for their own plans, swore to harvest everything at dawn before the poor arrived, without exception. The sheikh notes that giving is an acquired taste, and that the sons thought they had inherited an orchard when their real inheritance was their father's ethic of generosity. While they slept, Allah burned the land bare, mirroring their own plan to strip it. He explains key words: harvesting meaning to pick and pack for sale, and hard meaning to take and withhold, condemning those who use a stewardship that was never theirs to deprive others. The burning was an act of mercy that brought them to repentance before death. The middle brother's call to glorify Allah shows tasbih means seeing all good as coming from Him and never blaming Him. The surah frames Quraysh as tested in the same way, heirs of Ibrahim's legacy who abandoned it, with the Prophet sent as their lifeline. He closes by urging listeners never to stop a good legacy, illustrated by his grandfather's chickens.

outline.heading: The first story the Companions heard
outline.gist: Surat al-Qalam came very early, so this was likely the first Quranic story revealed.

outline.heading: Setting: a burnt land in Yemen
outline.gist: The site in Yemen is still barren today; the time and faith of the people are uncertain, but their religion was still uncorrupted.

outline.heading: The generous father
outline.gist: Every season he opened his vast orchard to the poor after Fajr and only harvested and sold what remained.

outline.heading: Giving is an acquired taste
outline.gist: His three sons did not share his love of giving; finding joy in giving takes time and discipline.

outline.heading: A story of ethics after a code of conduct
outline.gist: The surah first lists traits the Prophet must not have, whose opposites describe his character, then tells this story of ethics.

outline.heading: They inherited a value, not an orchard
outline.gist: Young and full of plans, the brothers resented their father's giving and fed each other's grievances.

outline.heading: The oath to harvest at dawn
outline.gist: They swore to pick and pack everything early with no exception, so they would not have to turn the poor away face to face.

outline.heading: Something from your Lord encircled it
outline.gist: The nature of the visitation does not matter; Allah answered their plan in kind, harvesting the land itself so nothing would ever grow.

outline.heading: It was never theirs
outline.gist: The father had learned over time that he was only a steward of Allah's land; the sons did not.

outline.heading: Setting out in whispers
outline.gist: They woke each other before light and whispered so no poor person would come today, showing a deliberate plan rather than a passing thought.

outline.heading: Able to withhold
outline.gist: Hard, used only here, means taking and keeping back from others; shame on using a stewardship to deprive.

outline.heading: The burning was mercy
outline.gist: Allah could have let them keep it and face account later; destroying it was a lifeline out of love.

outline.heading: We are lost; no, we are deprived
outline.gist: Like getting lost among Middle Eastern farm tracks at night, they first thought they took a wrong turn, then realised they had been deprived.

outline.heading: Why did you not glorify Allah?
outline.gist: The most faithful brother had misgivings; tasbih means seeing all good as from Allah and no flaw in Him, which they lost when greed broke the link with blessing.

outline.heading: Isa's subhanaka
outline.gist: Asked on the Day of Judgment about being worshipped, Isa begins by declaring Allah free of fault, the same refusal to blame Him.

outline.heading: Confession and blame
outline.gist: They admitted wrongdoing instead of blaming Allah, argued over whose idea it was, then called themselves transgressors.

outline.heading: Repentance and the greater punishment
outline.gist: They turned back to their Lord in time; without the loss they would have ended their father's legacy.

outline.heading: Continuing the father's legacy
outline.gist: Tafsir reports say they bought other orchards and carried on his generosity.

outline.heading: Quraysh tested in the same way
outline.gist: Quraysh inherited the legacy of Ibrahim and Ismail but thought they had inherited rule of Makkah; the Prophet was sent as their lifeline.

outline.heading: Never stop something beautiful
outline.gist: Cutting off a good legacy you hold is far worse than never starting one.

outline.heading: His grandfather's two chickens
outline.gist: An elderly man kept recalling the chickens his generous grandfather gave him, so the young imam finally delivered two himself.

outline.heading: Outro

39:53.ar: ۞قُلۡ يَٰعِبَادِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسۡرَفُواْ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ لَا تَقۡنَطُواْ مِن رَّحۡمَةِ ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَغۡفِرُ ٱلذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًاۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلۡغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
39:53.en: Say: O My slaves who have been prodigal to their own hurt! Despair not of the mercy of Allah, Who forgiveth all sins. Lo! He is the Forgiving, the Merciful

39:54.ar: وَأَنِيبُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمۡ وَأَسۡلِمُواْ لَهُۥ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن يَأۡتِيَكُمُ ٱلۡعَذَابُ ثُمَّ لَا تُنصَرُونَ
39:54.en: Turn unto your Lord repentant, and surrender unto Him, before there come unto you the doom, when ye cannot be helped

39:55.ar: وَٱتَّبِعُوٓاْ أَحۡسَنَ مَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡكُم مِّن رَّبِّكُم مِّن قَبۡلِ أَن يَأۡتِيَكُمُ ٱلۡعَذَابُ بَغۡتَةࣰ وَأَنتُمۡ لَا تَشۡعُرُونَ
39:55.en: And follow the better (guidance) of that which is revealed unto you from your Lord, before the doom cometh on you suddenly when ye know not

39:56.ar: أَن تَقُولَ نَفۡسࣱ يَٰحَسۡرَتَىٰ عَلَىٰ مَا فَرَّطتُ فِي جَنۢبِ ٱللَّهِ وَإِن كُنتُ لَمِنَ ٱلسَّٰخِرِينَ
39:56.en: Lest any soul should say: Alas, my grief that I was unmindful of Allah, and I was indeed among the scoffers

39:57.ar: أَوۡ تَقُولَ لَوۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هَدَىٰنِي لَكُنتُ مِنَ ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ
39:57.en: Or should say: If Allah had but guided me I should have been among the dutiful

39:58.ar: أَوۡ تَقُولَ حِينَ تَرَى ٱلۡعَذَابَ لَوۡ أَنَّ لِي كَرَّةࣰ فَأَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
39:58.en: Or should say, when it seeth the doom: Oh, that I had but a second chance that I might be among the righteous

25:68.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَدۡعُونَ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ وَلَا يَقۡتُلُونَ ٱلنَّفۡسَ ٱلَّتِي حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا يَزۡنُونَۚ وَمَن يَفۡعَلۡ ذَٰلِكَ يَلۡقَ أَثَامࣰ ا
25:68.en: And those who cry not unto any other god along with Allah, nor take the life which Allah hath forbidden save in (course of) justice, nor commit adultery - and whoso doeth this shall pay the penalty

25:69.ar: يُضَٰعَفۡ لَهُ ٱلۡعَذَابُ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ وَيَخۡلُدۡ فِيهِۦ مُهَانًا
25:69.en: The doom will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein disdained for ever

25:70.ar: إِلَّا مَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ عَمَلࣰ ا صَٰلِحࣰ ا فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ يُبَدِّلُ ٱللَّهُ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمۡ حَسَنَٰتࣲۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣰ ا رَّحِيمࣰ ا
25:70.en: Save him who repenteth and believeth and doth righteous work; as for such, Allah will change their evil deeds to good deeds. Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful

7:31.ar: ۞يَٰبَنِيٓ ءَادَمَ خُذُواْ زِينَتَكُمۡ عِندَ كُلِّ مَسۡجِدࣲ وَكُلُواْ وَٱشۡرَبُواْ وَلَا تُسۡرِفُوٓاْۚ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُسۡرِفِينَ
7:31.en: O Children of Adam! Look to your adornment at every place of worship, and eat and drink, but be not prodigal. Lo! He loveth not the prodigals

55:8.en: That ye exceed not the measure

2:143.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلۡنَٰكُمۡ أُمَّةࣰ وَسَطࣰ ا لِّتَكُونُواْ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ شَهِيدࣰ اۗ وَمَا جَعَلۡنَا ٱلۡقِبۡلَةَ ٱلَّتِي كُنتَ عَلَيۡهَآ إِلَّا لِنَعۡلَمَ مَن يَتَّبِعُ ٱلرَّسُولَ مِمَّن يَنقَلِبُ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيۡهِۚ وَإِن كَانَتۡ لَكَبِيرَةً إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ هَدَى ٱللَّهُۗ وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيُضِيعَ إِيمَٰنَكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِٱلنَّاسِ لَرَءُوفࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
2:143.en: Thus We have appointed you a middle nation, that ye may be witnesses against mankind, and that the messenger may be a witness against you. And We appointed the qiblah which ye formerly observed only that We might know him who followeth the messenger, from him who turneth on his heels. In truth it was a hard (test) save for those whom Allah guided. But it was not Allah's purpose that your faith should be in vain, for Allah is Full of Pity, Merciful toward mankind

17:15.ar: مَّنِ ٱهۡتَدَىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَهۡتَدِي لِنَفۡسِهِۦۖ وَمَن ضَلَّ فَإِنَّمَا يَضِلُّ عَلَيۡهَاۚ وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةࣱ وِزۡرَ أُخۡرَىٰۗ وَمَا كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتَّىٰ نَبۡعَثَ رَسُولࣰ ا
17:15.en: Whosoever goeth right, it is only for (the good of) his own soul that he goeth right, and whosoever erreth, erreth only to its hurt. No laden soul can bear another's load, We never punish until we have sent a messenger

12:87.ar: يَٰبَنِيَّ ٱذۡهَبُواْ فَتَحَسَّسُواْ مِن يُوسُفَ وَأَخِيهِ وَلَا تَاْيۡـَٔسُواْ مِن رَّوۡحِ ٱللَّهِۖ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يَاْيۡـَٔسُ مِن رَّوۡحِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلۡقَوۡمُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ
12:87.en: Go, O my sons, and ascertain concerning Joseph and his brother, and despair not of the Spirit of Allah. Lo! none despaireth of the Spirit of Allah save disbelieving folk

15:56.ar: قَالَ وَمَن يَقۡنَطُ مِن رَّحۡمَةِ رَبِّهِۦٓ إِلَّا ٱلضَّآلُّونَ
15:56.en: He said: And who despaireth of the mercy of his Lord save those who are astray

7:156.ar: ۞وَٱكۡتُبۡ لَنَا فِي هَٰذِهِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا حَسَنَةࣰ وَفِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ إِنَّا هُدۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَۚ قَالَ عَذَابِيٓ أُصِيبُ بِهِۦ مَنۡ أَشَآءُۖ وَرَحۡمَتِي وَسِعَتۡ كُلَّ شَيۡءࣲۚ فَسَأَكۡتُبُهَا لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ وَيُؤۡتُونَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
7:156.en: And ordain for us in this world that which is good, and in the Hereafter (that which is good), Lo! We have turned unto Thee. He said: I smite with My punishment whom I will, and My mercy embraceth all things, therefore I shall ordain it for those who ward off (evil) and pay the poor-due, and those who believe Our revelations

33:43.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي يُصَلِّي عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَمَلَٰٓئِكَتُهُۥ لِيُخۡرِجَكُم مِّنَ ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِۚ وَكَانَ بِٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ رَحِيمࣰ ا
33:43.en: He it is Who blesseth you, and His angels (bless you), that He may bring you forth from darkness unto light; and He is ever Merciful to the believers

6:12.ar: قُل لِّمَن مَّا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ قُل لِّلَّهِۚ كَتَبَ عَلَىٰ نَفۡسِهِ ٱلرَّحۡمَةَۚ لَيَجۡمَعَنَّكُمۡ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ لَا رَيۡبَ فِيهِۚ ٱلَّذِينَ خَسِرُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ فَهُمۡ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
6:12.en: Say: Unto whom belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and the earth? Say: Unto Allah. He hath prescribed for Himself mercy, that He may bring you all together to the Day of Resurrection whereof there is no doubt. Those who ruin their souls will not believe

6:54.ar: وَإِذَا جَآءَكَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا فَقُلۡ سَلَٰمٌ عَلَيۡكُمۡۖ كَتَبَ رَبُّكُمۡ عَلَىٰ نَفۡسِهِ ٱلرَّحۡمَةَ أَنَّهُۥ مَنۡ عَمِلَ مِنكُمۡ سُوٓءَۢا بِجَهَٰلَةࣲ ثُمَّ تَابَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ وَأَصۡلَحَ فَأَنَّهُۥ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
6:54.en: And when those who believe in Our revelations come unto thee, say: Peace be unto you! Your Lord hath prescribed for Himself mercy, that whoso of you doeth evil through ignorance and repenteth afterward thereof and doeth right, (for him) lo! He is Forgiving, Merciful

34:2.ar: يَعۡلَمُ مَا يَلِجُ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا يَخۡرُجُ مِنۡهَا وَمَا يَنزِلُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَمَا يَعۡرُجُ فِيهَاۚ وَهُوَ ٱلرَّحِيمُ ٱلۡغَفُورُ
34:2.en: He knoweth that which goeth into the earth and that which cometh forth from it, and that descendeth from the heaven and that which ascendeth into it. He is the Merciful, the Forgiving

24:31.ar: وَقُل لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ يَغۡضُضۡنَ مِنۡ أَبۡصَٰرِهِنَّ وَيَحۡفَظۡنَ فُرُوجَهُنَّ وَلَا يُبۡدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا مَا ظَهَرَ مِنۡهَاۖ وَلۡيَضۡرِبۡنَ بِخُمُرِهِنَّ عَلَىٰ جُيُوبِهِنَّۖ وَلَا يُبۡدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا لِبُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ ءَابَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ ءَابَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ أَبۡنَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ أَبۡنَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ إِخۡوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوۡ بَنِيٓ إِخۡوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوۡ بَنِيٓ أَخَوَٰتِهِنَّ أَوۡ نِسَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ مَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُهُنَّ أَوِ ٱلتَّٰبِعِينَ غَيۡرِ أُوْلِي ٱلۡإِرۡبَةِ مِنَ ٱلرِّجَالِ أَوِ ٱلطِّفۡلِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يَظۡهَرُواْ عَلَىٰ عَوۡرَٰتِ ٱلنِّسَآءِۖ وَلَا يَضۡرِبۡنَ بِأَرۡجُلِهِنَّ لِيُعۡلَمَ مَا يُخۡفِينَ مِن زِينَتِهِنَّۚ وَتُوبُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ جَمِيعًا أَيُّهَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ
24:31.en: And tell the believing women to lower their gaze and be modest, and to display of their adornment only that which is apparent, and to draw their veils over their bosoms, and not to reveal their adornment save to their own husbands or fathers or husbands' fathers, or their sons or their husbands' sons, or their brothers or their brothers' sons or sisters' sons, or their women, or their slaves, or male attendants who lack vigour, or children who know naught of women's nakedness. And let them not stamp their feet so as to reveal what they hide of their adornment. And turn unto Allah together, O believers, in order that ye may succeed

39:18.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَسۡتَمِعُونَ ٱلۡقَوۡلَ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ أَحۡسَنَهُۥٓۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَدَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُۖ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمۡ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
39:18.en: Who hear advice and follow the best thereof. Such are those whom Allah guideth, and such are men of understanding

7:145.ar: وَكَتَبۡنَا لَهُۥ فِي ٱلۡأَلۡوَاحِ مِن كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ مَّوۡعِظَةࣰ وَتَفۡصِيلࣰ ا لِّكُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ فَخُذۡهَا بِقُوَّةࣲ وَأۡمُرۡ قَوۡمَكَ يَأۡخُذُواْ بِأَحۡسَنِهَاۚ سَأُوْرِيكُمۡ دَارَ ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
7:145.en: And We wrote for him, upon the tablets, the lesson to be drawn from all things and the explanation of all things, then (bade him): Hold it fast; and command thy people (saying): Take the better (course made clear) therein. I shall show thee the abode of evil-livers

WM4DG8lGW5c.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat al-Zumar 39:53-58 (Do Not Despair of Allah's Mercy)
WM4DG8lGW5c.one_line: The verse of hope for those who wronged themselves: never despair of mercy, Allah forgives all sins, then turn back, submit and follow the best.
WM4DG8lGW5c.summary: He opens the closing section of al-Zumar, which he counts among the most beautiful passages in the Quran. After many verses that reasoned with the mind about sincerity, these speak to the heart, because the mind cannot be sincere while the heart holds someone else. The verse calling on those who have wronged themselves was revealed when people with a past of killing and sin asked whether Islam could still take them. He defines excess as doing more than benefits, even in worship, and reads 'O My servants' as a word of affection addressed even to the worst. Despair of mercy shows a failure to understand a mercy that encompasses everything, and it is Shaytan's favourite way in; forgiveness of all sins is a separate promise that sincerity unlocks. The story of Umar sending this verse to Hisham ibn al-As, who had lapsed, shows how it brings people home. He then reads the next verses as a road map: turn back to your Lord, hand your affairs to Him, and follow the best of what was revealed by ordering your priorities, fundamentals before details, so that the sudden arrival of the Last Day does not leave you with regret, blame or a useless wish to return.

outline.heading: The closing verses of al-Zumar deserve memorizing
outline.gist: Every commentator lingers over this final passage for its beauty; he urges people to memorize it and pray with it at night.

outline.heading: Sincerity, the greatest act of the heart
outline.gist: Sincerity is to the heart what tawhid is to outward deeds; the surah first argued with the mind and now ends by speaking to the soul.

outline.heading: Obedience needs a sincere heart, not only a convinced mind
outline.gist: The surahs from al-Ahzab onward ask for obedience in deeds, but the mind cannot be sincere while the heart is attached to someone besides Allah.

outline.heading: No project succeeds without mind and heart together
outline.gist: Nobody marries a person only because they are convinced on paper; Allah addresses both mind and heart because they rarely agree on their own.

outline.heading: Why the verse was revealed: sinners asking for a way back
outline.gist: People who had killed and sinned heavily asked whether Islam could still accept them; the verses of al-Furqan on repentance and this verse came as the answer.

outline.heading: What excess (israf) means
outline.gist: Excess is doing more of something than brings any benefit; eating past fullness is excess, while giving more good is not.

outline.heading: Even worship can become excess
outline.gist: Night prayer that ruins one's work and family duties is excess; the Prophet corrected Uthman ibn Mazun's withdrawal, so how much more our cars, houses and food.

outline.heading: Wronging yourself by enslaving it to other than Allah
outline.gist: To be excessive against yourself is to degrade a soul Allah honoured, making it a slave of money and desire; it harms you, not Him.

outline.heading: 'O My servants': a word of affection
outline.gist: 'Ibad' is a plural of love, 'abid' a plural of ownership; Allah calls even polytheists, disbelievers and sinful Muslims with tenderness.

outline.heading: Those too ashamed to tell what they did
outline.gist: People confide sins to him that could turn hair grey; his answer is this verse: nobody stands between a person and Allah's door.

outline.heading: The man who killed a hundred
outline.gist: Turned away by a worshipper and sent by a scholar to leave his land, he died on the way and was taken by the angels of mercy, perhaps because his heart had already left his past.

outline.heading: Despair is the door Shaytan uses
outline.gist: Only the lost and the disbelievers despair; Shaytan knows mercy encompasses everything, so he tries to convince you it cannot reach you.

outline.heading: A hundred parts of mercy
outline.gist: One part was sent down for all creatures' compassion and ninety-nine kept for the Day of Resurrection; on the Throne is written that His mercy prevails over His wrath.

outline.heading: The first hadith taught: show mercy and be shown mercy
outline.gist: The narration chained by 'firstness' is the first a student receives from a teacher; he holds several chains and a local teacher grants it too.

outline.heading: Despair means you misunderstood mercy
outline.gist: Mercy encompasses everything and you are a thing, so despairing of it contradicts what Allah declared; al-Rahman on the pattern fa'lan means mercy for all without exception.

outline.heading: He wrote mercy upon Himself
outline.gist: No one can oblige Allah, yet in al-An'am He twice decreed mercy on Himself, which makes despair impermissible.

outline.heading: Two separate promises, not cause and effect
outline.gist: Do not despair of mercy is one statement and He forgives all sins is another; mercy already reaches you, while forgiveness of every sin can come in a single moment.

outline.heading: Sins reaching the sky, and the secret of sincerity
outline.gist: The hadith qudsi of sins filling the earth met with equal forgiveness; a sincere heart is how all of them are wiped, as in the Prophet's dua for forgiveness that costs Allah nothing.

outline.heading: Always hope, and run to Him for forgiveness
outline.gist: Keep hoping that mercy will reach and rescue you, and hurry to ask forgiveness because He leaves no sin behind.

outline.heading: Why the Forgiving comes before the Merciful
outline.gist: Mercy is guaranteed and needs only that you not despair, while forgiveness needs repentance, so Allah puts it first to encourage it; Saba 34:2 is the one reversal.

outline.heading: Umar brings his household to Islam
outline.gist: After accepting Islam Umar gathered his family and refused to face them until they testified; he beat his son Abdullah for having hidden his Islam from him.

outline.heading: Umar sends this verse to Hisham ibn al-As
outline.gist: Hisham missed the agreed hijrah meeting and was pressured out of Islam; in Madinah Umar wrote him this verse, and Hisham read it weeping until he rode out to join the Prophet.

outline.heading: Reciting the next passage
outline.gist: He recites the verses on turning back, submitting, and the three regrets of the Last Day.

outline.heading: Interlude
A road map back for the one who strayed
outline.gist: After 'do not despair' come two more commands, turn back and follow, giving the sinner a way home.

outline.heading: Inabah is wider than tawbah
outline.gist: Repentance has its own heart and limb conditions; inabah is any good return to Allah, sometimes seeking forgiveness, sometimes changing one's whole life, a return of the heart.

outline.heading: 'Allah' for universal facts, 'your Lord' for the return
outline.gist: Mercy and forgiveness are stated with the name Allah because they hold for everyone; turning back is to 'your Lord' because it is personal.

outline.heading: The Lord is closer than a father
outline.gist: Rabb carries more than ab; a child is half from his father, while you are wholly from your Lord, so Allah uses Rabb when He draws people near.

outline.heading: Submit: hand the matter over to Him
outline.gist: Islam here is to leave your mercy, forgiveness and fate with Him and accept what He accepts; no one enters Paradise by deeds alone, not even the Prophet.

outline.heading: Follow the best of what was revealed
outline.gist: All revelation is good; the best is the command that best achieves Allah's purpose in the situation, and choosing it takes sincerity rather than appetite.

outline.heading: Using a divine command to hurt people
outline.gist: Rebuking someone publicly in the name of sincere advice can push them from Allah; the best way is the one that helps the person.

outline.heading: Following the best means ordering priorities
outline.gist: Start with tawhid, leaving the major prohibitions and the five pillars, then parents and kin, before details; a beard with haram income has the order upside down.

outline.heading: Why the sudden arrival matters
outline.gist: If the end comes while you were working down the list in order, you were not negligent; postponing the essentials for item 150 is what leaves you exposed.

outline.heading: First regret: alas for what I neglected toward Allah
outline.gist: 'That a soul should say' means lest it say; it regrets wasting its relationship with Allah while treating the warnings as a joke.

outline.heading: Second: blaming Allah for not guiding me
outline.gist: Unable to blame itself, the soul blames Allah, an ugly claim dressed up as talk of decree.

outline.heading: Third: if only I had another chance
outline.gist: It asks to rewind and do it right; none of regret, blame or the wish to return will help, which is why the verses command hope, return, submission and following now.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Intention and sincerity (niyyah, ikhlas)
themes.note: Sincerity is the summit of the heart's worship; obedience fails unless the heart joins the convinced mind.

themes.label: Tawbah: repentance and returning to Allah
themes.note: No sinner is beyond return; the verse answered people with heavy pasts and brought back a companion who had lapsed.

themes.label: Moderation and balance (wasatiyyah)
themes.note: Excess is doing more than benefits; even night prayer and asceticism can become excess when they crowd out duties.

themes.label: Hope, fear and the balance between them
themes.note: Despair is Shaytan's entry and a sign of misunderstanding mercy; hope must always remain.

themes.label: The Names and Attributes of Allah
themes.note: Al-Rahman means mercy for all, al-Ghafur is placed first to encourage seeking forgiveness, and Rabb is closer than a father.

themes.label: The companions and the early generations
themes.note: Umar's care for his family and friends, and his letter that brought Hisham ibn al-As back.

themes.label: Priorities in the deen: fundamentals before details
themes.note: Following the best of revelation means putting tawhid, the prohibitions and the pillars before outward details.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: The three useless responses of the soul on the Last Day: regret, blaming Allah, and asking to return.

quran.point: Revealed with 39:53 in answer to those asking whether killing and adultery could be forgiven; sins replaced with good deeds.
Eat and drink but do not be excessive, defining israf.
Do not transgress the balance, applied to balance even in worship.
A middle nation, knowing how not to do one thing at the cost of another.
Whoever is guided is guided for himself; your excess harms you, not Allah.
Only disbelievers despair of Allah's relief.
Only the astray despair of their Lord's mercy.
My mercy encompasses all things, so it encompasses you.
He is Merciful to the believers, the special mercy of al-Rahim.
He has decreed mercy upon Himself.
The second place where He decrees mercy upon Himself.
The one place where al-Rahim comes before al-Ghafur.
Turn to Allah in repentance, all of you, as the more specific command to repent.
Those who listen and follow the best of it, the earlier use of 'the best'.
The third place speaking of taking the best of revelation, with a different sense.

hadith.gist: Polytheists who had killed and sinned much asked the Prophet whether there was a way out if they accepted Islam, and the verses were revealed.
The Prophet told Uthman ibn Mazun he was not sent with monasticism: he fasts and eats, marries, prays and sleeps, and whoever turns from his sunnah is not of him.
The man who killed ninety-nine, then a hundred, was told to leave his land, died on the way, and was taken by the angels of mercy.
Allah created mercy in a hundred parts, sent one to earth and kept ninety-nine for the Day of Resurrection.
Written on the Throne: My mercy prevails over (or precedes) My wrath.
Show mercy to those on earth and the One above the heavens will show you mercy (the hadith chained by firstness).
Son of Adam, if your sins reached the clouds and you came to Me associating nothing with Me, I would forgive you and not mind.
The Prophet's dua: forgive us sins that do not harm You and grant us forgiveness that does not diminish You.
No one enters Paradise by his deeds, not even the Prophet, unless Allah covers him with His mercy.
The religion is sincere advice.

maxims: Mercy encompasses everything, and you are a thing
Despair of mercy is a failure to understand mercy
The mind cannot be sincere if the heart is not
Excess is doing more than brings benefit
Following the best means ordering your priorities

stories.who: The man who killed a hundred
stories.point: Nobody can block a sincere return to Allah; nearness is of the heart, not distance.

stories.who: Umar and his son Abdullah
stories.point: Umar's zeal for his family's faith; he resented that his son had kept his Islam from him.

stories.who: Umar and Hisham ibn al-As
stories.point: A friend's care and one verse of hope brought a lapsed companion back to Islam.

takeaways: Never let past sins convince you that Allah's mercy cannot reach you.
Return to Allah sincerely and seek forgiveness, knowing He can erase everything at once.
Keep balance even in worship so it does not crowd out work and family.
Order your practice: tawhid, avoiding major sins and the pillars before outward details.
Give advice in the way that helps the person, not the way that shames them.

62:2.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي بَعَثَ فِي ٱلۡأُمِّيِّـۧنَ رَسُولࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡ يَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ وَيُزَكِّيهِمۡ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَإِن كَانُواْ مِن قَبۡلُ لَفِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
62:2.en: He it is Who hath sent among the unlettered ones a messenger of their own, to recite unto them His revelations and to make them grow, and to teach them the Scripture and wisdom, though heretofore they were indeed in error manifest

62:3.ar: وَءَاخَرِينَ مِنۡهُمۡ لَمَّا يَلۡحَقُواْ بِهِمۡۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
62:3.en: Along with others of them who have not yet joined them. He is the Mighty, the Wise

62:4.ar: ذَٰلِكَ فَضۡلُ ٱللَّهِ يُؤۡتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَٱللَّهُ ذُو ٱلۡفَضۡلِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ
62:4.en: That is the bounty of Allah; which He giveth unto whom He will. Allah is of Infinite Bounty

62:5.ar: مَثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ حُمِّلُواْ ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةَ ثُمَّ لَمۡ يَحۡمِلُوهَا كَمَثَلِ ٱلۡحِمَارِ يَحۡمِلُ أَسۡفَارَۢاۚ بِئۡسَ مَثَلُ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِۚ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
62:5.en: The likeness of those who are entrusted with the Law of Moses, yet apply it not, is as the likeness of the ass carrying books. Wretched is the likeness of folk who deny the revelations of Allah. And Allah guideth not wrongdoing folk

62:6.ar: قُلۡ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوٓاْ إِن زَعَمۡتُمۡ أَنَّكُمۡ أَوۡلِيَآءُ لِلَّهِ مِن دُونِ ٱلنَّاسِ فَتَمَنَّوُاْ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
62:6.en: Say (O Muhammad): O ye who are Jews! If ye claim that ye are favoured of Allah apart from (all) mankind, then long for death if ye are truthful

62:7.ar: وَلَا يَتَمَنَّوۡنَهُۥٓ أَبَدَۢا بِمَا قَدَّمَتۡ أَيۡدِيهِمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمُۢ بِٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
62:7.en: But they will never long for it because of all that their own hands have sent before, and Allah is Aware of evil-doers

62:8.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ ٱلَّذِي تَفِرُّونَ مِنۡهُ فَإِنَّهُۥ مُلَٰقِيكُمۡۖ ثُمَّ تُرَدُّونَ إِلَىٰ عَٰلِمِ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَٱلشَّهَٰدَةِ فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
62:8.en: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Lo! the death from which ye shrink will surely meet you, and afterward ye will be returned unto the Knower of the Invisible and the Visible, and He will tell you what ye used to do

62:1.ar: يُسَبِّحُ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ ٱلۡمَلِكِ ٱلۡقُدُّوسِ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡحَكِيمِ
62:1.en: All that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth glorifieth Allah, the Sovereign Lord, the Holy One, the Mighty, the Wise

2:47.ar: يَٰبَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱذۡكُرُواْ نِعۡمَتِيَ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَنۡعَمۡتُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَأَنِّي فَضَّلۡتُكُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
2:47.en: O Children of Israel! Remember My favour wherewith I favoured you and how I preferred you to (all) creatures
